correctness.rationale: For all integers b>=3,m>=2 the real PSD Gram identity zT Mhat z=sum ||Eλ diag(z) Eλ||F² is proved from spectral idempotence; arrowhead coupling with nonzero sine sums yields simple coupled eigenvalues with hub support, and the even-mode cosine resolvent excludes spectral collisions since λ(λ-2)<8<b(m+1). Even path-mode compressions force per-blade sine-squared moments zero, and odd mode compressions on 1_b^perp force the same when b>=3. DFT inversion annihilates the symmetric blade components, while simple coupled eigenvectors force z0=0. The converse confirms all compressions vanish for antisymmetric blade vectors, giving exact nullity b floor(m/2). The independently constructed numerical checker exercises 40 graphs, 10 sine-squared rank tests and 30 resolvent identities; the unrestricted conclusion rests only on the proof.

value.rationale: The result proves the at-least-three-blade branch of an explicitly stated 2023 conjecture for an unbounded family of quantum-walk graphs, not merely recomputing the known finite table. The complete kernel identifies precisely the mirror-antisymmetric transport modes lost under long-time mixing, explaining the rank deficiency structurally. The theorem is a complete classification of a natural network family and requires distinct spectral-degeneracy and Fourier-compression arguments beyond a textbook projector formula. Remaining one-/two-blade cases are explicitly excluded.
